{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced by the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review, but NOT a new idea: this question already exists as PROSE in docs/requirements-coverage.md ("Note: are embeddings (an embeddings-rs sidecar) actually needed?"). Recording it here moves it from a document into the graph, which is the direction dec:what-lives-where argues for; it does not settle it. STILL OPEN.

WHAT IS AVAILABLE AND UNUSED: dynograph-vector ships an HNSW approximate-nearest-neighbour index (HnswConfig / HnswIndex / SearchResult, with filtered, batch and snapshot-persisted search) plus SIMD cosine similarity and the whole distance family. reflow2 uses none of it. search_design is BM25 lexical, and the schema carries embedding_field declarations on several node types that nothing populates.

THE CASE FOR: semantic search would find a requirement whose words differ from the query's. It would also strengthen resolution — the duplicate-detection path already has a fuzzy_then_vector strategy declared in the schema with the vector half unimplemented.

THE CASE AGAINST, and it is why this has stayed parked: embeddings need a MODEL, and reflow2-core is deliberately LLM-free and deterministic. An embedding provider at the core would break that, and putting it at the seam means a sidecar to install, version and keep in sync — which cuts against req:thin-install and the whole served-not-installed posture. Determinism is also load-bearing here: two runs of a detector must agree, and an ANN index is approximate by construction.

--- 2026-08-04, re-examined while building BL-186 (cap:corpus-ingest). Four things are now MEASURED rather than supposed, and one distinction is offered against the case-against. The question is still open and this update does not settle it. ---

1. THE PRODUCER EXISTS AND IS ANTHONY'S OWN. `embeddings-rs` (github.com/sligara7/embeddings-rs, local at a990e4d v0.1.1) is a Rust/ONNX parity sidecar for nomic-embed-text-v1.5 with a code-derived, drift-gated OpenAPI contract, written to pair with dynograph-foundation. That matters to the case-against: "a provider dependency" and "a local, self-hosted, contract-frozen sidecar you maintain" are not the same risk, and the deferral's stated reason was avoiding an external LLM provider.

2. THE WHOLE PATH EXISTS AND IS INERT — VERIFIED, not read from the earlier note. dynograph-storage has an embeddings column family with set_embedding / get_embedding / delete_embedding / scan_embeddings_by_type. dynograph-vector really does ship HNSW (crates/dynograph-vector/src/hnsw.rs) and SIMD cosine (distance.rs). reflow2's own schema declares embedding_field on Capability, Requirement, Question and others. reflow2's source contains exactly two matches for "embedding": a bidi-sanitizer comment and a doc comment saying "no embeddings". So the missing piece was never the model or the index — it is reflow2 calling any of it. embedding_field is another declared-and-read-by-nothing field, this time spanning four components.

3. NOT NEEDED FOR cap:corpus-ingest, AND ANTHONY SCOPED IT OUT ON 2026-08-04: "keep BL-186 lexical and ship it." The cost half of the corpus problem is candidate generation, which the BM25 index already in the served binary answers; embeddings would ADD a round trip per node, not remove one. The ordering half was a naming bug, fixed lexically. The folder driver needs no vectors.

4. WHERE IT WOULD ACTUALLY EARN ITS KEEP, and this is the honest limit of the lexical answer: req:corpus-ingest requires that "the same component named in forty specifications must converge on one node". Forty authors do not merely reorder tokens, they choose different words. token_sort_ratio cannot see "Read Cache" ~ "Local Store" at all — that is not a low score, it is invisible. The cases the scope doc names (Auth Service / Authentication Service = 84, Gateway / API Gateway = 74) are the EASY ones because they still share tokens. So shipping BL-186 lexical satisfies the requirement's ordering clause and its cost, and leaves its convergence clause satisfied only for documents that happen to share vocabulary. That limit should be stated to a user pointing reflow2 at a heterogeneous corpus rather than discovered by them.

5. THE DISTINCTION OFFERED AGAINST THE CASE-AGAINST: determinism is treated above as one blanket objection — "two runs of a detector must agree, and an ANN index is approximate by construction". That is strong for search_design and for anything feeding a gate. It is materially weaker for INGEST RESOLUTION, because under dec:ask-not-repair that path's output is a merge_candidate a human rules on, not a verdict. Approximate retrieval feeding a QUESTION is a different risk from approximate retrieval feeding a GATE. So the answer may not be a single yes/no: "yes, on the ingest resolution path only" would leave req:deterministic-core intact. Offered as a distinction to consider, not as advocacy — the req:thin-install objection stands unchanged either way, since a sidecar to install, version and keep in sync is a real change to the one-binary deployment story.

--- 2026-08-06: FIRST EXTERNAL EVIDENCE. Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 survey of the "graph brain" ecosystem (relayed by Anthony), recorded here because it bears on the case-against and on nothing else in the node. Does not settle the question. ---

6. EVERY COMPARABLE SYSTEM IN THE FIELD IS HYBRID, NOT LEXICAL. Mem0 combines vector search with graph relations and key-value storage; Cognee's pipeline is ingest, chunk, entity/relationship extraction, then vector DB plus graph DB plus relational, queried by hybrid graph-and-semantic similarity; Zep/Graphiti, Letta, LangMem and LlamaIndex Memory all rest on vector retrieval. Not one of the surveyed systems is retrieval-lexical-only. That does not make lexical wrong — none of those systems has reflow2's determinism requirement, because none of them feeds a GATE, which is precisely the distinction drawn in point 5 — but it does mean the case-against can no longer include "nobody needs this": everyone building in this space has paid for it. The question narrows to whether reflow2's gate-feeding, one-binary posture is worth the retrieval quality it costs, and that is a real trade rather than an oversight.

7. WHAT THE COMPARISON DOES NOT SHOW: none of those systems has to answer a query the same way twice, and none of them exports a byte-stable artifact a CI gate diffs. So their unanimity is weak evidence about reflow2's core and strong evidence only about the ingest-resolution path — exactly where point 5 already located the weaker objection.
